title: What surprised you
hook: the thing you didn't expect to learn

segments.voice: Yesterday: the world, languages and colors as signs, and one body. Your line was everywhere.

A boat pulls away from the shore with two travelers aboard. Once they're on board, one of them sets to work knocking a hole in its side. The other is Musa, a prophet, and he can't believe what he's seeing. In Surat al-Kahf he set out on this journey to learn, and promised his teacher, a servant of Allah given knowledge from Allah's own presence, that he would be patient. He lasts until the boat. You met this pair on day four hundred sixty-eight. Today, after a year of learning, the thing you didn't expect.
screen: `A HOLE IN THE BOAT.` → `A PROPHET WHO PROMISED PATIENCE.` → `WHAT YOU DIDN'T EXPECT.`

segments.voice: In the Qur'an's telling, the boat is only the beginning. Musa protests. Then comes a second act, far harder, and Musa cries out against it. Then, in a town that refused them food, the man rebuilds a falling wall for nothing, and Musa says he could at least have taken pay. Each time the man reminds him, in paraphrase: did I not say you could not be patient with me? Then the explanations. The boat belonged to poor people, and a king was seizing every boat by force; a damaged one would be passed by. Under the wall lay a treasure belonging to two orphan boys whose father had been righteous, kept safe until they were grown. What looked wrong was something Musa didn't yet know. Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari name the man al-Khidr; the Qur'an simply calls him one of Allah's servants. Musa was a prophet, and he still had more to learn, and the learning arrived as surprise. The Qur'an elsewhere gives the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, a line to say: "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge." Surprise can be what that request looks like when it's answered. And your own year? Maybe it was that hadith scholars tested the words as well as the chain. Or that, in Sahih al-Bukhari, Allah divided mercy into a hundred parts and sent down only one. Or that people of different schools stand in one row and no one corrects anyone. Or something else entirely, that didn't go the way you expected.
screen: `A BOAT, A SECOND ACT, A WALL.` · `WHAT LOOKED WRONG WAS NOT YET KNOWN.` · `INCREASE ME IN KNOWLEDGE.` · `WHAT DID THIS YEAR SURPRISE?`

segments.voice: Let the year go by slowly, like pages turning: the pillars, the reports, the schools, the creed, the heart, the manners, the life cycle, the world. Somewhere in there one thing may catch, a moment of wait, really? Not the most impressive one, the one that actually caught: hold it for the rest of the sit, and find the one sentence that says it.
What surprised you. The moment a year of learning went somewhere you did not expect, which in Musa's story is where the learning really began. Today's word.
Your line: surprised. In Musa's story, that's where the learning began. That's day one thousand four hundred twenty.

howItsDone: Muslims read the story of Musa and al-Khidr in Surat al-Kahf, which some recite on Fridays, and teachers use it to speak about humility in learning and the limits of what a person can see.

chat.says: Why did Musa keep objecting if his teacher was right all along?
options: He didn't yet know what lay behind each act, like the orphans' treasure under the wall.
Because the teacher was wrong, and the Qur'an sides with Musa in the end.
Because Musa already knew everything and was only testing his teacher.
chat.meaning: What looked wrong was something Musa did not yet know: a damaged boat a king would pass by, a treasure kept safe for two orphans.
